newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Amnesty nets big haul of Taiwan gangsters.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty nets big haul of Taiwan gangsters.

text.p: A total of 1,528 Taiwan gangsters have turned themselves in to police during an amnesty, officials said on Thursday.

"By the close of our Wednesday deadline 1,528 people had registered with police, renouncing their affiliations with the underworld, or disbanding the triad gangs they had formed," a spokesman of the Justice Ministry told Reuters.
He said 597 inmates of prisons in Taiwan had also renounced their gang affiliations, while 44 triad gangs had disbanded during a two-month grace period that started on December 13.
Under the amnesty, gangsters who turn themselves in will not face charges of being a gang member but can still be prosecuted if they had committed crimes.
A police report issued before the amnesty said that out of Taiwan's population of 21 million, a total of 10,582 people were gangsters belonging to 1,236 gangs.
Taiwan lawmakers passed an anti-gangster law last November after a mass slaying in which a county magistrate and seven other people were killed by two gunmen.
The killings, followed shortly by a rape-murder of a prominent feminist, led to public outcries against the government.
Business leaders expressed concern, saying deteriorating law and order would discourage foreign and domestic investment.
In an effort to eliminate organised crime, judicial authorities announced on December 13 the two-month grace period for gangsters to report themselves to police and renounce their gang affiliations.
"The amnesty programme was aimed at giving a chance to gangsters who want to start a new life," Justice Minister Liao Cheng-hao said on television on Thursday.
"But for those who want to use this as a cover and continue to engage in criminal or gang activities, we would ask for double punishment against them if they are caught," Liao warned.
Taipei prosecutors on Thursday arrested three professional baseball stars who were alleged to have thrown games in exchange for cash from gangsters running gambling rackets.
